title: A perfect Hausa safety proxy masked low-quality responses in one model assessment
summary: In a 500-prompt Hausa safety evaluation, Gemini classified every base Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct response as safe—the paper’s refusal-rate proxy—but rated 96.2% low quality. Model variants changed benign-request over-refusal and judged linguistic quality by different amounts.
organization: African Institute for Mathematical Sciences; Bayero University Kano; University of Hamburg; Imperial College London

source_review.scope: §§4–6, evaluation conditions, Table 3 and single-judge limits

evidence.tested: Five model variants answered 500 harmful and 200 benign Hausa prompts. One Gemini judge rated safety, helpfulness and linguistic quality using a structured rubric.
evidence.unknown: Many prompts were translated, and the ratings did not receive independent native-speaker validation. The results concern this benchmark and its one automated judge. The harmful-prompt judge returns SAFE/UNSAFE; its reported refusal-rate proxy does not independently authenticate a coherent Hausa refusal.
evidence.ai_role: The tested learned models produced Hausa responses; the learned judge supplied separate safety and language-quality ratings rather than using refusal counts alone.
